## The question

[How to remove white space between image and shape for visual alignment in LaTeX when using tikz and graphicx?](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/726676/how-to-remove-white-space-between-image-and-shape-for-visual-alignment-in-latex), asked by [Fabio Corradini Santander](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/340378/fabio-corradini-santander) on TeX Stack Exchange (2024-09-17; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> When I place an image at the top of the page using the page as a reference, there's a white space between the page border and the image. When I then place a rectangle to the left of the image, using the image's top-left corner as a reference, the rectangle is separated from the image by a white space, but there's no white space between the top of the page and the rectangle. As a result, the two items are not visually aligned. I'm not sure whether this white space is added by ```graphicx``` or ```tikz```, but I suspect it's ```graphicx```. I want to remove the white margin to align both figures relative to each other.
>
> ```latex
> \documentclass{article}
> \usepackage[paperwidth=216mm,paperheight=280mm]{geometry}
> \usepackage{graphicx}
> \usepackage{tikz}
>
> \begin{document}
>
> \begin{tikzpicture}[remember picture, overlay]
> 	\node[anchor=north] (head) at (current page.north)
> 		{\includegraphics[width=10cm]{head}};
> 	\draw[black] (head.north east) rectangle ++(3.5,-4.2);
> \end{tikzpicture}
>
> \end{document}
> ```
>
> [![Image and rectangle not aligned][q-1]][q-1]
>
>
>   [q-1]: 9nEoHTPK.png
:::

Actually this is added by `tikz`. The node has some separation around it, which keeps (for example) a box drawn around the edge from crashing into the contents.

If you add `inner sep=0pt` to the `\node` options, you will see it disappear.

See Section 17.2.3 of the PGF/TikZ 3.1.10 manual.
